proposals.title: Where your missed questions are: the gap to target, split by skill
proposals.what: A new full-width card #gap. On desktop it gets its own row right after next | mist; on a phone it comes second, after #next. Header: WHERE YOUR MISSED QUESTIONS ARE. Headline: 'On a 44-question section you miss about 17 now. 700 means missing about 7.' Below that, the top 6 skills are shown as rows, and 'Show all 19' expands the rest in place. Each row shows: the topic chip; '~2.1 of 3.1 questions missed a section'; a bar split into expected right and expected missed; 'could win back ~1.4'; '3 open mistakes'; 'last worked 12 days ago'; and a .btn 'Work on this · 10' (POST /api/drill {topics:[t], count:10, source:'today'}). A sort toggle offers 'Most questions first' (the default) and 'Quickest wins', which puts rows with open traps first. A named mistake closes in two clean answers. A skill with fewer than 5 answers gets an 'unmeasured' tag and uses its domain's mean. Helper line: 'Approximate. The SAT publishes domain shares, not skill shares, so a domain is split evenly across its skills.' Server: estimate.gap(learner). per_section(t) = 44 x domain share / topics in the domain, which gives Algebra 3.1, Advanced 5.1, PSDA 0.94 and Geo 1.65 per skill. p(t) = accuracy over the last 40 non-repeat answers, reweighted to module 1's 7/8/7 easy/medium/hard mix. missed = per_section x (1 - p). winback = max(0, missed - per_section x 0.15), that is, the gain from reaching Strong. allowed = 44 x (1 - frac), with frac from inverting scoring.ANCHORS. /api/today adds gap:{now_missed, allowed, rows:[{topic, domain, per_section, p, missed, winback, traps, answered, measured, last}]}. Up next's reason line quotes it: '~1.4 missed questions a section in these skills · 3 open mistakes'. The student works on the skills that hold the most missing questions, not the ones they like or the ones the week happened to bring. The target becomes a number they can count toward ('miss 7, not 17'), and every session starts with its value stated. Their score rises faster because the minutes go where the marginal points are.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Score Progress shows one number and a target, which read 0 until a full test and out of sync with their wizard. Their plan's 'Score gap: 1000 now, 1400 target' tile is a subtraction. Nothing they show says where the missing points are or which skill is worth the next hour. Their 'Why this task?' is free-text AI copy with no numbers.
proposals.needs: F4 estimate.py (R16) for the target and band; progress.board (mastery, answered, traps); BLUEPRINT and scoring.ANCHORS (both exist); S3 coach reason line. Plan (S7) could read the same rows for its slot allocation so the two never disagree.

proposals.title: I have N minutes: one tap builds the best session for the time you actually have
proposals.what: At the top of Up next there is a .choices row 'I have: 5 · 10 · 20 · 30 · 45 · 60 min'. It defaults to what is left of today's goal (at least 5), or 20 when no goal is set. Under it, a composition preview: a stacked bar plus one line per block, for example: '20 min · 13 questions: 2 check-ins due (Circles, Percentages) · 3 recalls · 3 mistake repairs · 5 new, mixed: Probability, Nonlinear functions'. Each block row has an x that removes it; its time goes back to 'new'. The pill reads 'Start · 20 min'. Seconds per question come from the learner's own median ms over their last 20 answers in each topic, clamped to 45-180 s, or 95 s without data. The server builds it with coach.compose(learner, minutes, tz), filling time in this order: check-ins due (R9, up to 30%); recalls due (see the recall proposal, up to 20%); open traps ordered by the gap ledger (up to 30%); new questions on the top two ledger skills, interleaved (the rest, at least 30%); and one keep-warm question on a Strong skill idle for 10 or more days, when 20 minutes or more are chosen. 5 min is labelled 'Streak saver' and holds only check-ins and traps. It is offered as the first choice after 18:00 local time when nothing has been done today. The drill body gains blocks:[{pool, ids|topics, count}] (F5 validates each block as a sub-body). POST /api/drill/preview {compose:minutes} returns the blocks. The session serves blocks in order, with new and redo mixed. When the budget runs out it offers 'Your 20 minutes are up · Finish · 5 more'. With an active plan, the blocks are today's plan tasks, trimmed to the minutes by dropping the lowest points-per-minute tasks first. The student starts every day in one tap, sized to the day, instead of skipping a day that can't fit the planned 60 minutes or picking comfortable topics. Every minute goes first to spaced retrieval and named-mistake repair, the cheapest points, then to interleaved new practice. That is the order the spacing and interleaving research supports, and it makes busy days count, so consistency rises.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep asks for daily time once, in the plan wizard (30 to 240 min chips), and their generator failed 3 of 3 times. Their dashboard offers their plan's checkbox tasks or a generic question of the day; nothing lets a student say 'I have 15 minutes' and get the best 15 minutes.
proposals.needs: F5 drill body 'blocks' and preview; R9 check-ins due; attempts.ms per topic; the gap ledger for ordering; S7 plan.today_summary tasks with minutes and value for the plan case; S4 session 'budget reached' footer.

proposals.title: Still got it? Spaced recall of everything you got right, with a 14-day due forecast
proposals.what: R9 brings back only fixed mistakes, at 3, 10 and 30 days. This extends spacing to every question type the student has solved. A clean first-try right answer on a template schedules a recall at +3 days. Each clean recall advances the stage (3, 10, 30, 60 days). A miss drops it to stage 0 (due tomorrow) and opens a trap as usual. Anything due after the exam is pulled to 5 days before it, as a last pass. Stored in a new table recall(learner, template, stage, due, last), updated in progress.record. progress.recall_due(learner, tz) returns [{template, topic, due, stage}] plus forecast[14]. Pool review gains due:true, which serves due templates on fresh seeds, oldest due first. On Today, the Review card (#mist, R30) changes its due line to 'Due today: 2 check-ins (fixed mistakes) · 6 recalls (types you had right)', with one .btn 'Do all 8 · 10 min'. Under that, a list of the due topics, each with a memory word: Fresh (inside its interval), Due, Fading (overdue by more than twice its interval). For example: 'Circles · right 3 of 3 · last seen 16 days ago · Fading'. The Today list gets a row 'Recall · 6 due · 7 min' that ticks itself when done. The calendar's future cells show '4 due' from the forecast, and the day detail lists them. The student spends 5 to 10 minutes a day answering new versions of question types they already solved, at growing intervals, instead of only practising what is new or broken. The testing effect and spacing keep a skill from week 1 alive on test day. Without it, 'Strong' skills decay silently and leak points in the section. The generator makes every recall a new question, so recalling never turns into remembering an answer.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has spaced repetition only for vocabulary ('Due Today N' in My Words, which stayed at 0 after grading). Their Math practice never brings back a solved type, and a fixed bank could only bring back the same question with the same answer.
proposals.needs: F4 recall table and progress.record hook; F5 pool 'review' with due; R9 check-ins, shown in the same row; F1 UI.calendar forecast marks; S10 Review's CHECK-INS DUE uses the same wording; the time-box proposal uses recalls as a block.

proposals.title: Pacing profile: speed against accuracy per skill, with speed sets and careful sets
proposals.what: A new card #pace: on desktop a full row after #study, with four quadrants side by side; on a phone after #mist. The headline projects a module: 'At your speed a 22-question module takes about 41 min. The clock is 35: about 4 questions would go blank or be rushed.' It is computed as the sum over skills of per_module(t) (half of the ledger's per_section) x the learner's median seconds, with unmeasured skills at 95 s. The four quadrants use each skill's last 30 days (5 or more non-repeat answers with ms): 'Banked' (median 95 s or less, 70% or more right); 'Speed up' (over 95 s, 70% or more right); 'Slow down' (60 s or less, under 70% right); 'Learn first' (over 95 s, under 70% right). Each lists its topic chips with the median, e.g. 'Systems 2:40'. Actions: 'Speed set · Systems · 10' sends POST /api/drill {topics:[t], count:10, timing:'custom', minutes: ceil(10 x max(80, median-20)/60)}, with the pace alert at that target. The summary then shows 'median 2:40 -> 1:58'. 'Careful set · Percentages · 8' is untimed. Before each question it shows the student's last fast wrong pick on that type ('Last time: 0:38, picked: added the percentages'). /api/today adds pace:{module_minutes, over_questions, rows:[{topic, median_ms, acc, n, quad}]} from progress.pace(learner), the same median function as Plan's slow-skill rule (median over 120 s times a skill). The student learns which skills cost them the clock and trains those under a shrinking per-question target. They also see which skills they rush and miss. SAT Math gives 35 minutes for 22 questions. A slow-but-right skill turns into blanks or rushed guesses at the end of a module, and a fast-wrong skill is slips. Both lose points with no content gap, and no amount of content study fixes them.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's report payload has no time per question at all. Their QBank stopwatch resets on reload. Their only time analysis is the contest 'average seconds per answered question, by difficulty', which was empty. Nothing on their dashboard mentions pace.
proposals.needs: attempts.ms (exists; tests via R7 qstate ms into record_paper); the gap ledger's per_section; S4 custom timing plus the per-question pace alert (in Practice spec); S7 sharing the median helper.

proposals.title: Test post-mortem: where the points went, split into causes, each with its own fix
proposals.what: On every finished test card on Today (and in the report hero, via S6's sitting card), the single 'Fix 13' becomes a split: '13 missed: 6 concept · 3 slips · 3 out of time · 1 grid-in entry', drawn as a stacked bar with a legend. Definitions, computed in /api/history rows as lost:{concept, slip, time, entry, blank}. Time: blanks when the module ended on the clock, plus wrong answers given in under 20 s in the module's last 5 minutes. Entry: a grid-in where the new scoring.entry_error(given, key) returns short_decimal (value within 0.01 of the key but too few digits: 0.66 for 2/3, which grid_equal already rejects), mixed_number ('1 1/2' equal to 3/2), too_long (more than 5 characters positive or 6 negative), or unit (a % or unit typed). Slip: wrong on a topic with 80% or more first-try right over its previous 20 answers (R9 kind 'slip'). Concept: every other wrong answer. Each part has its own .btn. Concept: 'Fix 6' (pool redo, from_session, only those qids). Slip: 'Careful set · 8' on those topics. Time: 'Pace set · 10' on the module's slowest topics. Entry: 'Grid-in entry · 5', grid-ins whose keys are fractions or repeating decimals, with the rule shown after each. A toggle 'Retest these in 2 days' writes retests(learner, session, due). On that day the Today list shows 'Retest Sep 21's misses · 13 fresh versions' (fresh seeds on the missed templates) and ticks itself when done. Test-to-test deltas per domain sit under the band: 'Algebra +3 right vs Sep 14'. After a test, the student treats the four causes differently: study the concept, slow down, pace, fix the entry format. They no longer 're-read all the explanations', which spends the hour on material they already know. The 2-day retest is spaced retrieval of exactly what the test exposed.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Recent Tests card is TOTAL SCORE, R&W, Math and Review. Their results list puts wrong and blank answers in one red chip, their report gauge counts blanks as wrong, and their payload has no time per question. They cannot tell a time loss from a content loss, and nothing is retested.
proposals.needs: S6 /api/history modules with wrong/blank (R26, R35) plus the lost split; R7 qstate ms and timestamps for tests; R9 slip kind; a new scoring.entry_error beside grid_equal; F5 pools; a retests table (F4); S6 sitting card renders the split everywhere.

proposals.title: Confidence tap and blind spots: know when to trust your first answer
proposals.what: Every answer hosted on Today gets an optional three-way tap before Check: 'Sure · Not sure · Guess' (K cycles it). That covers the day's questions, Try one now and the time-boxed set, and practice gets it through a pref 'confidence' (default on for Today, off elsewhere). It is stored as attempts.conf (sure|unsure|guess; guess also sets R8 guess=1). Rules in progress.record: sure-and-wrong opens the trap as kind 'blindspot' with owed 3. It sorts to the top of the Review card with the tag 'You were sure'. unsure-and-right opens owed 1, which is R9's existing 'unsure'. A calibration strip in the Review card, shown once 20 or more answers are tagged: 'Last 30 days · Sure: 86% right (58) · Not sure: 54% (24) · Guess: 30% (10)', with one reading line. Sure at 90% or more: 'Trust your sure answers on test day and spend the saved time on the not-sure ones.' 75-89%: 'Mostly reliable: re-check sure answers only on the last step.' Under 75%: 'You miss 1 in 4 answers you are sure of: re-read what the question asks before choosing.' The day's-questions crowd line adds 'People who were sure got it right 71%'. The student commits to a confidence before seeing the key and learns whether their 'sure' can be trusted. Their confidently wrong mistakes, which they would never review because they think they know them, get extra repair. On test day they spend flag-and-return time where it pays.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has no confidence data anywhere. Their QOTD is a one-shot right or wrong, and QBank's unlimited retries make even their accuracy meaningless. Our Tests spec puts Sure/Unsure/Guess in the exam only, off by default. Today makes it the daily habit and the place where calibration is read.
proposals.needs: F3 UI.workspace confidence control in inline and practice modes (the exam control exists in the Tests spec); F4 attempts.conf column and the record() rule; R9 kind 'blindspot'; R11 prefs key 'confidence'; S3 crowd split by conf in daily.py.

proposals.title: Your mistake patterns: one habit across many skills, drilled across skills
proposals.what: The Review card (#mist) gets a segmented 'By mistake · By pattern' control. By pattern groups open and 30-day traps by norm (R8/R9; Review's norm-to-templates index already finds 79 misconceptions shared across templates). For example: 'Changed the sign of the slope · 5 times · in Linear functions, Two-variable data, Systems', with a .btn 'Pattern drill · 8'. That sends POST /api/drill {pool:'related', ids:norm, count:8}, which serves items across templates where one option names the misconception (via want), so resisting the trap is practised in every skill it lives in. Above the list is a 30-day cause line from R9 kinds: '11 concept · 6 slips · 2 grid-in entry · 3 blind spots'. Each count links to its drill: slips to a careful set, entry to the grid-in entry set, blind spots to redo with those ids. The student sees that four 'different' mistakes are one habit and fixes the habit once, not one topic at a time. Fixing a pattern closes points in every skill it appears in. A per-topic list hides that one error is costing points in several places.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's dashboard shows no mistakes at all. Their review modal's 'Distractor Analysis' is prose about one question, never added up, and their redo API has no UI. A bank without labelled distractors cannot group mistakes by cause.
proposals.needs: R8 attempts.norm; S10 norm index and pool 'related' (F5 want); R9 kinds; the blindspot kind from the confidence proposal.

proposals.title: Worked-example pairs for new and stuck skills: study one solved, then solve its twin
proposals.what: The coach flags a skill as new (under 3 answers) or stuck (mastery under 0.3 after 6 or more answers). When Up next's set contains such a skill, the set starts with two worked pairs for it. The reason line says so: 'New skill: Circles · starts with 2 worked examples'. Pair 1: a worked card showing the stem, the key marked, the rationale, and 'Traps on this type', with each wrong option's misconception (Item.reasons). One button, 'Got it · try one', follows, then the same template on a fresh seed to answer. Pair 2 fades the support: the next template shows only 'Traps to avoid' before the student answers, with no rationale. After that, plain practice. Inside any set, a .quiet 'Show me one solved' in the question strip puts a worked twin of the current question's template before it. The current question stays unanswered and still counts. Worked seeds are db.remember-ed so they are never served as questions, and worked cards file no attempt and do not move mastery. Drill cfg gains worked:n (F5). The workspace gains a read-only 'worked' mode (F3). With a new skill, the student studies a solved example with its traps named, then solves the twin. They don't guess through the first questions and pile up mistakes that then have to be un-learned. The worked-example effect is strongest for novices, and naming the traps first stops misconceptions from forming. Only a generator gives an exact, unlimited twin for every example.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep teaches nothing before asking. Explanations appear only after an answer, their QOTD never shows the key, and a fixed bank cannot make a twin of the example it just showed.
proposals.needs: F5 cfg 'worked' (serve n worked cards per flagged template, remembered, no attempt filed); F3 workspace 'worked' mode; S3 coach flags new/stuck and the reason line; S4 'Show me one solved' in the question strip.

proposals.title: Measure what we cannot see yet: an 8-question skill check for unmeasured skills
proposals.what: The gap card and the Score card both list unmeasured skills (under 5 answers): 'Unmeasured: Probability, Circles, Margin of error, Statistical claims · they hold about 5 questions a section · your band is wider because of them'. A .btn 'Measure them · 8 questions · 12 min' sends POST /api/drill {pool:'untried', topics:unmeasured, each:2, adaptive:true, source:'measure'}: two questions per skill, starting at medium, stepping up after a right answer and down after a miss (R33). On finishing, the summary and Today show each one move from unmeasured to a measured row in the ledger ('Circles: ~0.6 of 1.65 missed a section'). The coach stops using domain-size order for those skills. The estimate's confidence reason (R16) adds 'N skills unmeasured' and drops it once they are measured. In 12 minutes the student gives the coach data on the skills it is guessing about. The next week's practice then targets real leaks. A never-tried skill can be the biggest leak, and priorities are only as good as the measurement behind them.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's plan wizard makes the student self-rate each domain Focus, Normal or Strong. Their estimate drops floor-score sections, and nothing measures skill by skill, so their plan's priorities rest on a guess.
proposals.needs: progress.board answered per topic; F5 pool untried with each and adaptive; the gap ledger; F4 estimate.py confidence reason.

proposals.title: Readiness for test day, and a taper in the final two weeks
proposals.what: The SAT countdown card (#exam) gains a READINESS list headed '3 of 6 ready'. Each row is computed and, when unmet, has its own action: 'Every skill practised: 17 of 19' (links to the 8-question measure); 'Timed full sections in the last 6 weeks: 1 of 3' (Start section); 'Pace: your median 1:52 a question, SAT pace 1:35' (Pace set); 'Open mistakes in big skills: 5' (Fix); 'Check-ins and recalls due: 8' (Do all); 'Grid-in entry errors this month: 2' (Grid-in entry). Without a plan, Up next switches to taper order in the last 14 days: timed mixed sets at the module difficulty mix, check-ins and recalls, and a one-time 'Last pass' drill over every mistake fixed since the student began (fresh seeds). There are no new skills in the last 3 days. The eve reads '15 minutes: your 5 most-missed mistakes, one each, then stop.' Exam day shows only the checklist. With a plan, Plan's Final phase (S7) drives Up next and the readiness list only reports. The student sees what 'ready' means in concrete terms and closes the unmet items. The last two weeks go to consolidation, timing and relapse checks instead of cramming new material. Full timed sittings build pacing and stamina, and the last pass catches fixed mistakes that have come back.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's countdown is a DD:HH:MM:SS clock with a date select that still offers past dates. It never says whether the student is ready or what the remaining days should hold.
proposals.needs: the pace, measure and recall proposals; R9 check-ins; F4 estimate sittings count; S7 Final phase (Plan owns the taper for plan users, and Today must not contradict it); S3 coach taper branch.

proposals.title: What your time bought: progress stated in questions, not minutes
proposals.what: The Study card (#study) gains a section 'WHAT YOUR TIME BOUGHT' with a This week | This month toggle. One row per skill worked: 'Percentages · 1h 10m · 41% -> 78% right · ~+1.2 questions a section · 3 mistakes closed', sorted by gain. Mastery before comes from mastery_of over the attempts before the period, the same as the week recap's 'before'. Questions a section come from the gap ledger. A totals line: 'This month: 6h 20m · ~+3.5 questions a section · 14 mistakes closed'. A 'Comfort time' line appears when over 30% of the period's minutes went to skills already Strong at the time: 'Comfort time: 35% of this week went to skills you already have', with 'Put it on Probability instead' (a set on the top ledger skill). After each finished session, Up next shows one line: 'Last set: Circles 6/8 · 38% -> 52% · 1 mistake closed'. A consistency figure sits next to the streak: '5 of the last 7 study days met your goal', and a broken streak does not zero it. Once today's goal is met, a .quiet 'Tomorrow at 17:00 · 30 min? Add to calendar' offers a single .ics event with an alarm (UI.ics(event)), a time and a length the student commits to. The student sees which hours moved their score and which were comfort, and moves the comfort time to weak skills. They come back because progress shows in the unit that matters. Consistency and a stated time for tomorrow keep daily practice going better than a streak that resets.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep shows study minutes today and this month, and a streak pill that disagrees with the profile. Their achievements are four hard-coded tiles with a dead 'View All'. Minutes alone say nothing about whether the practice worked.
proposals.needs: F4 progress.days minutes per topic (attempt ms); mastery_of at a date (as the spec's week.moved); the gap ledger's per_section; F1 UI.ics(event); S7 plan streak rules for rest days (R13).

When behind, show what a shorter day would drop: 'At 30 min a day the plan keeps the fixes and check-ins and drops 2 new-skill sets' (lowest points per minute first). The student then knows the cost of each choice.

parity_gaps.spec_says: The band, a route tag, right/asked, a mini scale, missed-question chips (wrong vs blank), Review, Fix N and New one like this.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Theirs shows the score and Review. Our chips and Fix bring the report one tap closer, but the card still treats every lost point the same way.
parity_gaps.upgrade: The lost-points split (concept, slips, out of time, grid-in entry, blank), each with its own fix. A 'Retest in 2 days' toggle that puts fresh versions of the misses on the Today list on that day. Per-domain deltas against the previous test.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Three labelled streaks from single sources, with the best streak, consistent across pages; rest days don't break the study streak (R13).
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: A streak pill is their mechanic. Three of them is more of the same number, and a streak that resets to zero after one missed day is the moment students quit.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Put a consistency figure next to the streak ('5 of the last 7 study days met your goal') that a broken streak cannot wipe out. Offer the 5-minute 'Streak saver' (check-ins and traps only) after 18:00 local time when nothing is done. After the goal is met, ask 'Tomorrow at 17:00 · 30 min?' and add it to the calendar, a commitment that raises follow-through.

parity_gaps.spec_says: The four steps as links, a preview from the student's data, three bullets, 'Free, as many as you like', Build my plan.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their CTA's shape (eyebrow, title, three bullets, one button). The preview helps, but building still means going through a four-step wizard.
parity_gaps.upgrade: A one-tap plan: 'Start from 540 -> 620 · Oct 3 · 35 min on the 5 days you actually studied · focus: Nonlinear functions, Percentages', with every value prefilled from the estimate, the gap ledger, the next official date and the student's 14-day average minutes and weekdays. 'Use this plan' builds it at once, and 'Change' opens the wizard at step 1.

proposals.title: Where your points are: price every skill in questions per test, and let that pick Up next
proposals.what: Server: new progress.stakes(learner) returns [{topic, domain, share_q, p, lost_q, traps, answered, unseen}] plus total_lost_q. share_q is how many of a 44-question section the skill gets: the domain's count from blueprint.DOMAIN_SPLIT (15/15/7/7) times the skill's share of its domain, taken from the College Board QBank skill counts in the teardown table (e.g. Nonlinear functions is 258 of Advanced Math's 538, so about 7.2 questions; Evaluating statistical claims is 12 of 420, so about 0.2). p is smoothed first-try accuracy, (right + 2·p0)/(answered + 2), with repeats left out (R8), p0 the domain's accuracy, weighted to the module tier mix 7/8/7. lost_q = share_q × (1 − p). Unseen skills use p0 and are drawn hatched. Today: the Score card's 4 domain rows (§9 Domains) become WHERE YOUR POINTS ARE: the top 5 skills by lost_q as horizontal bars (ink length = lost_q; orange dots = open traps; hatched = not tried yet), mono `2.9 q a test`, the mastery word, and a `.btn` `Practice · 12 q` that sends POST /api/drill {topics:[t], count:12}. `All 19 skills` expands in place into a sortable table: skill, share of test, % right first try, open mistakes, q lost per test, last worked. Summary line: `Across skills you drop about 13 of 44 questions a test. The top 3 hold 6 of them (roughly +60 to +90 points).` Points use a stated 10 to 15 points a question around the student's band, and the helper says so: `Rough: first-try accuracy × how often the SAT asks each skill. A guide to where your time pays, not a score.` Up next: coach() orders by lost_q × (1 + 0.5·min(traps,3)) plus the existing keep-warm lift. The reason line reads `About 2.4 questions a test at stake · 3 open mistakes`. A `.quiet` `Swap` cycles in place through coach.ahead[1..4], each shown with its own value (`Circles, Lines & angles · 1.6 q`), with no trip to the builder.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's dashboard gives only `Score gap · 1000 now, 1400 target`, and its plan Progress tab ranks `Accuracy by domain, weakest first` by % right, ignoring how often the SAT asks each skill. At 20% right, Evaluating statistical claims costs about 0.2 questions a test; at 60%, Nonlinear functions costs about 2.9. Their domain copy is also mislabelled (`13% of test section, 1-8 questions`). Ours says where the points are, in the units a test is scored in, and starts that set in one tap.
proposals.needs: F4: progress.stakes() next to progress.board(), plus a topic-weight constant alongside blueprint.DOMAIN_SPLIT (a stated heuristic like scoring.ANCHORS; add it to open question 12). F5/F4: coach() reorders by stakes. S7 can reuse stakes for Plan step 4 focus suggestions and the week theme. /api/today gains `stakes`. S6 Results can show the same table.

proposals.title: Start today: one tap runs the whole Today list back to back
proposals.what: When the Today list has 2 or more undone rows, Up next's pill reads `Start today · 3 parts · ~46 min`. Minutes come from the student's median seconds per question (else 95 s). A `.btn` `Only the set` sits beside it. Part order: the open drill or the plan/coach set, then the unanswered day's-question slots, then Words due (when S9 is present and due > 0), then the challenge, offered as an opt-in. The chain is stored in sessionStorage `satf.chain = {day, parts, i}` (try/catch). At the end of each part, the session summary (S4) shows an interstitial above its usual content: `Part 1 of 3 done · 31/38 right · 2 mistakes closed`, then `Next: Day's questions · 2`. The pill `Continue` is also Enter; `Back to Today` is Esc. The day's questions run inside the runner in UI.workspace inline confirm mode and post to /api/qotd with ms. The challenge interstitial reads `Challenge · ranked · 10 q · 16 min` with `Start` / `Not today`. A 3-segment labelled rail at the top shows where the student is in the day. If the student leaves mid-chain, Up next reads `Continue today · part 2 of 3` and the list keeps each row's own progress. The chain ends on the Day receipt (next proposal). Step count for plan set + both day's questions: TopTierPrep takes about 12 taps and 3 screen changes outside the questions themselves (task, session with no end screen, Go Back, Answer, pick, Check answer, Show explanation, Done, twice, then a manual Mark done). Ours takes 1 tap and 2 Enters.
proposals.beats: Their Today's Plan card launches one task at a time, and their QBank session has no end screen, so the student has to find the way back. Each question of the day is its own modal with its own Done, and every task needs a manual tick. Ours is one continuous run that ticks itself.
proposals.needs: S4: a chain hook in the session summary, next to Plan's existing `Next in today's plan` hook. F3: UI.workspace inline mode for the QOTD part. S3: order the parts from /api/today.plan (S7 plan.today_summary) or the coach. S9: words due deck URL. S8: challenge start route. R24: the chain's QOTD/inline parts are never listed as sittings.

proposals.title: Day receipt: what today bought, shown once when it's earned
proposals.what: When every counted task is done, or minutes reach profile.minutes (whichever comes first), Up next turns into the receipt for that day. The day ring fills once as entry-only motion, off under reduced motion. It shows: `Day done · 46 min · 41 questions · 78% right (+6 on your 7-day average)`; `Closed:` with each closed misconception named as a chip linking to /review/?open=trap:<id> (`Added the percentages instead of multiplying them`); `Moved:` Percentages Learning → Getting there ▲; `Won back about 0.6 questions a test` (the stakes delta, from the first proposal); `Study streak 5 · best 9`; and `Tomorrow: Circles & Probability · 22 q · ~35 min` with `Add to calendar` (UI.ics event at prefs.study_time). Actions: pill `Keep going · 10 more` (next coach set), `.btn` `Copy summary` (UI.copyText, plain text for a parent or tutor) and `.quiet` `Share progress link` (R18a). After the first view it collapses to one line at the top of Up next (`Day done · 46 min · 3 closed ›`), which expands again on tap. It never appears for a day with no real completion, and there is no confetti.
proposals.beats: Their finished state is an `All Done 🎉` badge. Their QBank has no session summary at all, so they never tell a student what the time achieved. Ours names the mistakes closed and the skills moved, and says what tomorrow holds.
proposals.needs: S3: /api/today.receipt {minutes, questions, right, avg7_pct, closed:[{id,label,topic}], moved:[{topic,from,to}], stakes_won_q, streak, best, tomorrow:{title,count,minutes,topics}}. It is built from progress.days, traps closed today and mastery_of before/after (already needed for week.moved). tomorrow comes from S7 plan.today_summary(next day) or coach.ahead[1]. F1 UI.ics, UI.copyText. S1 progress link.

proposals.title: Plan from my data: a ready plan in one tap, with the wizard as Adjust
proposals.what: The no-plan CTA (§8) shows a finished plan built from defaults instead of three bullets. Exam date: the profile's, else the next official date at least 28 days away. Minutes: the median of the student's active-day minutes over 14 days rounded to a chip, else 45. Days: the weekdays they actually studied in the last 3 weeks, else Mon to Fri. Focus: the 2 domains with the highest lost_q. Target: the latest band's middle plus a Steady pace × weeks, rounded to 10 and capped at 780. It reads: `Your plan, ready: Oct 3 · 45 min × Mon–Fri · focus Advanced Math, Data · target 640 (Steady, +12 a week)`, followed by the first day's tasks from POST /api/plan/preview (`Today: Fix 3 mistakes · Focus set 18 q · ~35 min`). The pill `Start this plan` sends one create call; Today repaints Up next into plan mode in place and shows the toast `Plan started · Undo`. `.btn` `Adjust` opens /plan/?step=1 with every value prefilled. Each default is a tappable chip that opens its own small popover (date, minutes, days), so one change costs one tap and not a wizard. A brand-new student sees the same card with neutral defaults, plus `Or start from a score: Diagnostic · 20 q`.
proposals.beats: Theirs is a 4-step wizard, one generation per billing cycle, and a fake 5-step build screen. Their generator failed 3 times out of 3 on the re-walk, and `Try again` reset the draft. Ours goes from no plan to a running day in 1 tap, and every default can be seen and changed.
proposals.needs: S7: POST /api/plan accepts {defaults:true} or a body the client builds from /api/plan/preview; plan.mirror keeps learners fields in sync (R15). F4: progress.days for minutes and weekday inference; stakes for focus. S7 pace tag constants for the target.

proposals.title: Final week, exam eve, exam morning, after: Today reshapes itself around the test
proposals.what: The modes are driven by S7 plan.state (active | eve | exam | after), or by days_left with no plan. FINAL WEEK (7 to 2 days left): Up next's reason reads `Final week: no new skills, only your mistakes and check-ins`, and the coach pool is limited to redo and checks. The countdown card gains READINESS, 4 bars with text: `Top 5 mistakes closed · 3 of 5`, `Pace: last timed section 1:31 a question (test 1:35) ✓`, `Grid-in: 78% right on your last 20`, `Dress rehearsal: not yet`. Dress rehearsal: `.btn` `Rehearse Saturday at 8:00 AM` puts a UI.ics event in the calendar (Math section · 70 min). A timed section started between 7:45 and 8:30 local on a Saturday is tagged `Rehearsal ✓` in its cfg and on the card. EVE: Up next reads `Rest. Tomorrow, doors close at 8:00 AM.`, with an optional `.btn` `Warm-up · 5 you've got right before` (pool seen, right, easy), and the checklist opens. EXAM MORNING: only the checklist, the doors timer and a 3-question easy warm-up, with the line `No new work today.` AFTER: `How did it go?` with three one-tap choices (Better than practice · About the same · Worse), stored; `Add your official score` (source Official); and the plan CTA for the next date with its pace (`Nov 7 · 35 days · Steady`).
proposals.beats: Their countdown ticks DD:HH:MM:SS to an unstated time and nothing on the dashboard changes as the test gets close. Their picker still offers past dates. Ours turns the last week into a taper with a rehearsal at the real start time and a readiness read-out from the student's own data.
proposals.needs: S7: plan.state and a final-week phase whose pool is redo+checks. F4: estimate.py (pace from sessions.qstate ms, R7), traps top 5, grid-in accuracy from attempts. S5: a `rehearsal` tag on section cfg. F1: UI.ics. S3: store the after-test feeling (a learners column or prefs key). Open question 10: the 8:00 AM time and checklist wording need checking.

proposals.title: Day's questions show time: you vs the crowd vs test pace, and how fast the trap was taken
proposals.what: After Check, each slot adds a mini timeline from 0:00 to 3:00. It marks test pace 1:35 (dashed), the crowd's median (ink tick), the fastest 10% (faint tick) and the student's own time (orange dot), with mono labels. The copy depends on the result. Right and fast: `Right in 0:52, faster than 70% of today`. Right and slow: `Right, 25 s over test pace. The quick way:` followed by the rationale's first step. Wrong on a trap: `You picked B in 0:31. People who chose B took 0:40 on average, so the trap is the answer that looks quick.` Each option row's crowd bar also gets that option's mean time in mono (`B · 23% · 0:40`). Grid-in's top wrong values carry their mean time as well. All crowd timing appears only once the day has at least 20 on-time answers. Before that the line reads `You're one of the first 12 today`.
proposals.beats: Their QOTD records no time. Their report payload has no time per question at all, so nothing tells a student they are right but too slow for the test. Showing that the trap is the quick answer needs per-option timing on named distractors, which only our bank has.
proposals.needs: S3: POST /api/qotd already sends ms. Add crowd.ms {median, p10, by_option:[..], by_value} computed over on-time qotd attempts, with the 20-answer threshold (open question 12). F3: an actions/extra slot in UI.workspace for the timeline. F1 charts: a tiny `UI.paceLine`, or reuse UI.spread.

proposals.title: Fix 3 now: an inline mistake stack in the Review card, not a one-question sheet
proposals.what: The Review card's primary becomes `.btn` `Fix 3 now · ~3 min`. On desktop the card itself turns into a mini runner: the top trap's fresh-seed question renders in the card; A–D or 1–4 picks, Enter checks, and the verdict names the misconception with the rationale's first line. The owed pips fill in place, and the stack moves on after Enter (or after 1.5 s when right, off under reduced motion). A closed mistake's row slides out of the top-5 list, and the card's big open count ticks down live. End line: `3 answered · 2 closed · 1 needs one more clean answer`, with `3 more` / `Done`. On a phone the stack is a full-height bottom sheet with the options in the lower half, 44px rows. The stack is sized 3 by default, and `5` / `All` are offered after the first stack. It replaces the spec's one-question Try one now dialog; the per-row `Fix · 2 questions` stays.
proposals.beats: Theirs has no mistakes view on the dashboard, and redo exists only in their API (`Redo Questions 0` on the profile). Ours closes named mistakes in about a minute each without leaving Today, on questions no student has seen before, because a generator can make a new question of the same misconception on demand.
proposals.needs: F5: POST /api/drill {mistakes:true, templates:[top 3], count:3, source:'try'} with cfg.inline (R24). F3: UI.workspace inline mode with keyboard. S10: /api/review/counts to repaint the card. S3: refetch /today on Done.

proposals.title: A Today keyboard scope: Enter starts studying, J/K walks the cards
proposals.what: Register UI.keys scope `today`; §2.8 has none for this page. Keys: `Enter` with nothing focused runs Up next's primary (Start / Continue / Resume / Start today). `J` / `K` move focus card to card, in DOM order, with a 2px ink focus ring on the card, and `Enter` runs the focused card's primary. `D` jumps to the first unanswered day's question; there A–D / 1–4 pick and Enter checks. `F` opens the Fix stack. `C` starts or resumes the challenge. `E` opens the exam-date popover. `T` opens the target sheet. `?` lists them under This page. On pageshow back from a session, focus lands on Up next's pill, so Enter continues. On a fine pointer, Up next's footer shows the hint `Enter to start · J K to move · ? keys` in mono 11px; the hint is hidden once the student has used a key 3 times (localStorage try/catch). The keys are ignored while typing and when prefs.keys is off, as §2.8 says.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has no keyboard support on its dashboard, and its popovers even ignore Esc. For a returning student, studying starts with one key.
proposals.needs: F2: UI.keys supports a page scope and card focus. S3: registers the map and sets aria-keyshortcuts on each primary. F2: the `?` sheet shows the Today scope.

proposals.title: Instant Today: paint from last-known data, keep showing it through failures
proposals.what: Each card's last good payload is kept in localStorage `satf.today.{learner}`: /api/today, /api/qotd, /api/challenge, /api/history slice, /api/calendar month. It is stored with the local day, inside try/catch. On load with the same local day, every card paints from cache in the first frame. Skeletons show only on a first visit or a new day. Revalidation runs in parallel; changed numbers swap in place with one 150 ms cross-fade, and the layout never shifts. If a call fails, a card that has cached data keeps it and adds a mono line `As of 9:14 AM · Retry` in place of blanking to `Couldn't load this.`. A card with no cache shows the spec's error. Cached QOTD never carries keys, since the server withholds them until answered anyway. On idle, `<link rel=prefetch>` fetches /practice/session/, runner.js and question.js, so Start opens straight away. Writes (skip, goal, target, date) are optimistic with Undo and revert on failure, as the spec does for marks. The target: return visits interactive in under 150 ms.
proposals.beats: Their dashboard reloads to skeletons on every visit, and failures surface as a transient toast (`Could not start task. Please try again.`). Ours opens drawn, and a flaky connection costs a timestamp, not the page.
proposals.needs: F2: UI.api gains {cache:key} (same pattern as the shell's satf.shell sessionStorage cache in Shell §2.12). S3: per-card paint from cache. No server change.

proposals.title: Thumb-first phone Today: a grid-in key row, a docked Up next, swipeable question slots
proposals.what: (1) Grid-in on phones: the input uses inputmode=decimal, and an accessory row of 44px keys sits under it: `−` `/` `.` `⌫` `Check`. They insert at the caret and follow the same keystroke filter. iOS's decimal pad has no minus or slash, so without the row a student can't type -3/4. (2) Docked Up next: when #next scrolls out of view (IntersectionObserver), a 52px row joins the top of the fixed tab bar with the primary (`Continue · 7 of 38 ›`). The page's bottom padding grows by 52px, so nothing is covered (rule 6 holds). It hides while an input has focus or when #next is back in view. (3) Day's questions: the tabs stay, and a horizontal swipe on the question body (40px threshold, never starting on an option) switches slots. (4) The calendar collapses to the current week row with a `Month` toggle, and the day detail sits under it. (5) Every sheet is a bottom sheet with its primary in the lowest 25% of the screen.
proposals.beats: Their dashboard is a desktop layout with a 220px sidebar. Their QOTD is a centred modal, and their vocab button floats over content. Ours puts every primary within thumb reach, and a phone student can actually enter negative and fraction grid-ins.
proposals.needs: F3: the grid-in field's accessory row in UI.workspace (shared with the session and runner on touch). F2: the shell's tab bar exposes a dock slot. S3: observer and swipe on Today. F1: UI.calendar week mode.

proposals.title: Monday review: one weekly decision point in place of banners that pop up at random
proposals.what: On the first visit on or after the week's start (prefs.week_start), a `LAST WEEK` block sits above the next action in Up next. It holds UI.barChart of the 7 days' minutes against planned (outlined bars), `124 questions (+30) · 71% right (+4) · 3h 10m of 3h 45m`, `6 mistakes closed · 2 new`, the skills that moved (up to 3 ▲ and 2 ▼ as chips), and a score change when a new sitting landed. Under it is exactly one decision, whichever applies first. Behind: `Make study days 30 min`, with Plan's preview line `Ends the same date · 8 fewer questions a day`. Drift: `Update your plan's start to 610`. Target reached: `Raise target to 740?`. Neither: `Same again this week`. Each applies with a toast Undo. `Dismiss` collapses the block into the spec's `This week vs last` line in #study. Behind and drift then appear only here and in their home cards, never as interrupting lines on other days.
proposals.beats: Their adaptive banners (fallen behind, score drift) fire whenever a threshold trips, and `Not now` just snoozes for 3 hours. They have no week on the dashboard at all. Ours turns the adjustment into a calm, scheduled weekly check-in with evidence and a one-tap, undoable change.
proposals.needs: S7: behind {planned, done, suggest_minutes}, suggest (drift, R16), POST /api/plan/preview, PATCH plan. S3: /api/today.week (already specced) plus a last-seen-week marker (S1 /seen or localStorage). F1: UI.barChart.

proposals.title: Keep the streak, the fair way: an evening save and earned milestones
proposals.what: After prefs.study_time + 2h (else 19:00 local), on a study day (not a plan rest day, R13) with no activity yet and a study streak of 2 or more: the hero's streak chip turns ink-bold, and Up next gains a top line `Your 6-day streak ends at midnight. One answer keeps it.` with `.btn` `Keep it · 1 question`. The button scrolls to and focuses the day's MC question, since one answer makes a study day under R13. The midnight grace (R13) still applies to the day's question. Milestones at 7, 30, 60 and 100 study days, and `every planned day this week`, earn a one-time rise of the flame chip (entry-only) and a toast `7-day streak · your best yet` linking to the achievement (R25). Plan rest days show on the calendar as neutral grey ticks, so a student can see the streak was not broken.
proposals.beats: Their streak pill (QOTD: 1 day) disagrees with their profile (Streak 0 Days), and nothing helps a student keep it. Ours is one number, respects rest days, and gives a one-tap save that is also real practice.
proposals.needs: F4: progress.days (streak, rest-aware). F4 prefs.study_time. S1: achievements.py streak rules and the shell toast. S3: the evening condition on the client clock.

proposals.title: Calendar that explains itself: planned vs done in every cell, and when you do your best work
proposals.what: Plan days in UI.calendar get a 2px bar along the cell's bottom: an outline for planned minutes and an ink fill for done, over the existing heat. The month header reads `18 of 22 study days · 9h 20m of 11h planned`. The day detail adds `.btn` `Redo this day's misses (4)`: a drill of fresh seeds on the templates missed that day, open or not. A new line `WHEN YOU DO YOUR BEST WORK` sits under the calendar. It shows first-try accuracy for 4 time blocks (before 12, 12–17, 17–21, after 21) and for 7 weekdays as small bar pairs, only when each shown block has at least 40 answers. One insight line picks the gap when it is at least 8 points: `You get 78% right before 5 pm and 63% after 9 pm.`, with `.quiet` `Set study time to 16:00`, which writes prefs.study_time and moves the .ics reminder.
proposals.beats: Their calendar cells are buttons that do nothing and are drawn in UTC. They record a Preferred Time (Evening) that affects nothing. Ours makes each day actionable and tells a student when their accuracy is actually better.
proposals.needs: F1: UI.calendar planned/done bar. S3: /api/calendar adds planned minutes per day (from S7 plan days) and missed templates per day. F5: POST /api/drill {from_day} (fresh seeds of that day's wrong templates) in the drill body. F4: accuracy by local hour and weekday from attempts.at (X-Tz).

parity_gaps.spec_says: §2: `WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 23`, `Good morning, Aziz`, 4 status chips (streak, minutes, SAT in N days, plan N of M).
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: The greeting and date are their hero word for word. The chips are four facts that the cards below repeat, so the biggest type on the page still says nothing new.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Put one computed briefing sentence under the greeting, chosen by state. Plan day: `10 days to go. Today's 45 min is Probability and Circles, where 2.4 questions a test are slipping.` Back after a gap: `Welcome back. Since Sunday: 2 check-ins came due and your challenge closed at #4 of 37.` New score: `Your module came in at 560–640, 40 up on the last one.` Add up to 3 `Since your last visit` event chips (new score, contest result, check-ins due, assignment due), each linked, from S1 /api/me/feed and /seen.

parity_gaps.feature: Day's questions: two side by side, select then Check, one attempt
parity_gaps.spec_says: §5: MC + grid-in side by side at ≥1080, confirm mode (tap selects, Check sends). The spec itself says `Theirs has the same Check step.`
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: The layout (two columns) and the answer flow (select, Check, one try) are theirs. The reveal is better, but the moment of answering is identical.

After the reveal, sure-and-wrong reads `You were sure: this is a blind spot`, which opens the mistake with kind unsure. Right-but-not-sure also counts as unclean (R8/R9). A monthly line on the card: `Sure and wrong 3 times this month, all percent-of-percent traps`. Add a crowd scope switch after answering: `Everyone · Your class · Same SAT date` (S2 members, learners.exam_date). Add the time benchmark (proposal 6).

parity_gaps.spec_says: §5 header: flame + `3 days in a row` / `Start a streak`.

parity_gaps.upgrade: Add best, milestones and the evening one-tap save (proposal 12). On the past-days strip, mark graced answers with a small moon tick and late answers with a hollow mark, so the student sees exactly why a day did or did not count.

parity_gaps.feature: Up next count and clock controls
parity_gaps.spec_says: §3a: `.choices` 5 · 10 · 22 · {coach} · Endless, plus a Timed/Untimed toggle, meta `{n} questions · {min} min`.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: This is their QBank bottom bar (Volume 10/20/30/40/50/All, Mode Timed|Untimed) moved onto the dashboard: the same two decisions, counted in questions.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Size the set by time, the way students think: `10 · 20 · 35 · 60 min · Endless`, with a live `≈ 14 questions at your pace` from the student's median first-try seconds (else 95 s). Timed means `at test pace`, with the pace alert. Count stays under More options. Add `Swap` (proposal 1), so changing topics costs one tap and no builder.

parity_gaps.feature: Today's plan list: N of M, minutes left, All done, Full plan, Why, Skip, Move, Practice again
parity_gaps.spec_says: §3b: `PLAN · 1 of 2 done · 22 min left of 60`, rows with status box, type tag, meta, Why, Start/Continue, ⋯ Skip / Move to…, auto-completion.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Apart from auto-ticking, the row anatomy and action set are their bundle's (Why this task?, Skip, Mark done, Practice again, Undo, Move to).

proposals.title: Points map: where your next points are, ranked by points per minute, one tap each
proposals.what:
A new card `#gain` directly under Up next. Desktop: `gain x8 | pace x4`. Phone: right after `#next`. Header: `WHERE YOUR NEXT POINTS ARE`, with a quiet `How this works` popover on the right.

Top line: `If you sat a section today: 540-620` (a model, stated as one), plus the confidence word from R16 and `Harder module 2: 58% likely`.

Under it, up to 6 lever rows ordered by gain per minute. Each row has:
- the topic glyph and a lever tag: `Open mistake`, `Weak skill`, `Grid-in gap`, `Slow` or `Route`
- one specific line, e.g. `Added the percentages instead of multiplying · caught 3x`
- the gain in mono (`+10`, rounded to 5 and shown only when 5 or more)
- the cost (`3 questions · 4 min`)
- a `.btn` `Work on it`, which POSTs the lever's drill body with source 'gain': a trap sends {pool:'redo', templates:[t]}; a weak skill {topics:[s], count:10, adaptive:true}; a grid-in gap {topics, formats:['spr'], count:8}; slow sends the speed drill of the pace card; route sends {topics, tiers:['medium'], count:10}.

Footer:
- `Your +140 gap: the top 6 cover about +70` when a target is set.
- `All 19 skills` expands in place to a sortable table: gain, gain/min, mastery word, accuracy, open traps.

Model, in `estimate.forecast(learner, at=None)`:
- Cell accuracy for each (topic, tier) is shrunk toward the crowd: p = (right + 6*p_crowd) / (n + 6), over the learner's last 40 answers. Repeat, disputed and void rows are left out, and a guessed right counts 0.5. p_crowd is everyone else's first-try accuracy on that cell, with the fallback {easy .78, medium .55, hard .30} under 50 answers.
- The learner's spr/mcq ratio (shrunk to 1) multiplies the grid-in slots.
- The slots of `blueprint.slots('module1', 1)` and both module 2 forms are spread over each domain's topics by the official per-skill share.
- P(route up) is the Poisson-binomial chance of at least 14 of 22 in module 1. The centre is `P_up*c_upper + (1 - P_up)*min(c_lower, 580)`, using `scoring._interpolate`, with a band of ±70.
- When the learner's median time on each slot's topic adds up to more than 2,100 s, the last questions count as blank.

Levers:
- A trap recomputes its cell with that norm's misses removed.
- A weak skill takes p to min(p + .15, the crowd's 75th percentile).
- A grid-in gap sets the ratio to 1.
- Slow sets that topic's median to 95 s.
- Route is the cheapest +1 expected right in module 1, shown when P_up is between .25 and .75.

Cost is the questions needed (trap owed + 1; weak 10; grid-in 8; slow 6) times the learner's median ms on the topic.

New student: `Answer 30 questions to see where your points are · 12 of 30`, with a meter, and the blueprint prior line `Algebra and Advanced Math are 70% of the section`.
proposals.beats: Their `Score gap: 1000 now, 1400 target` tile is a subtraction. Their Score Progress reads 0 until a full-length test. Their plan's `Accuracy by domain, weakest first` ranks by percent, not by points, and names nothing to do. Ours says which named misconception or skill is worth how many points and how many minutes, and starts that drill in one tap. That needs every wrong answer attributed to a misconception on a template, plus fresh items on that template. A fixed, unlabelled bank has neither.
proposals.needs: F4 `estimate.py` (R16) gains `forecast()`. It needs an hourly-cached crowd prior over attempts, per topic x tier, first tries only, and the official per-skill shares as a constant. F5 drill body (R10) with source 'gain'. `blueprint.slots`, `scoring._interpolate` and `LOWER_ROUTE_CEILING` (read-only). /api/today gets `forecast`. The Help page (S1) takes the `How this works` copy. Plan step 4 (S7) and the Score card read the same levers, so there is one source.

The worksheet is regenerated from (template, seed), so the same link reprints identically for a tutor. Options: `Include answer key` (on), `Include explanations` (off), `Extra space for work` (on). Then `Print / Save as PDF` calls window.print().
proposals.beats: They have no print anywhere, and their Share / Export Report button has no handler. Only a generated bank can print an unlimited, never-repeating daily worksheet whose key explains why each wrong answer is tempting.
proposals.needs: S4 (Practice): the worksheet print view and 'end-mode set left in progress'. F6 sets codes (R18c) for the answers-later link. F1 print CSS in ui.css. F5 `parts` (the time-boxed set) for composition. R19 access so the key prints only in worksheet mode, never for live-test items.

proposals.title: Countdown that knows registration and score dates
proposals.what:
The `#exam` card shows a line under the date trigger: `Register by Sep 18 · late registration by Sep 22 · scores about Oct 16`.

- Within 7 days of the registration deadline, the hero SAT chip and the card show `Registration closes in 3 days`, with an external `Register with College Board` link.
- The date popover tags each official date `Registration open`, `Late registration only` or `Registration closed`, and sorts the closed ones last with a note.
- After the exam, the passed state reads `Scores usually arrive about Oct 16`. `Add your official score` comes back to the top of Today on that date.
- `Add to calendar` (UI.ics) adds the registration deadline as a second event.
proposals.beats: Their date combobox lists already-passed dates and shows only a ticking DD:HH:MM:SS. Deadlines are what students actually miss, and a countdown that ignores registration is decoration.
proposals.needs: F4 `server/satdates.py` adds `register`, `late` and `scores` per date, served in `/api/shell.dates` (R15). It must be verified against College Board before shipping (Part 5 Q10). UI.ics(event) for multiple events (F1 kit).
